# I18N-COVERAGE-SCAN — the ESLint rule's blind spots, enumerated

**Owner:** WS-SCAN. **Generated by:** `scripts/i18n-scan.ts` (`npx tsx scripts/i18n-scan.ts --json`).
**Snapshot date:** 2026-08-16, repo `91d1788a`, branch `swarm/ws-scan`.

`i18n/no-unkeyed-string` (`tools/eslint-rules/no-unkeyed-string.cjs`) guards `src/**/*.tsx`
against new hardcoded UI strings, and reports 0 active / 1,261 suppressed violations. That
number is the floor of the backlog, not the ceiling — the rule's own header and
`eslint.config.js`'s file scope document four classes of string it structurally cannot see.
This scan enumerates all four across the whole app (`src/**`, ~1,033 non-test `.ts`/`.tsx`
files) using the exact same `isAllowedString` / `ATOMIC_TERMS` / `TRANSLATABLE_ATTRS` /
`isIgnoredFile` definitions the real rule uses, so "translatable" means one thing everywhere
in this codebase.

## Headline totals

| Class | Count | `key-it` | `exempt-*` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1. `tmpl-expr` — interpolated template literals in a UI position | 82 | 82 | 0 |
| 2. `hoisted-const` — strings in hoisted `const` arrays/objects | 97 | 97 | 0 |
| 3. `non-tsx` — UI strings in `src/**/*.ts` (not `.tsx`) | 160 | 160 | 0 |
| 4. `ignored-file` — files exempt by `IGNORED_FILE_PATTERNS` | 232 | 0 | 232 |
| **Total** | **571** | **339** | **232** |

Classification breakdown: **339 `key-it`**, **157 `exempt-admin-dev`**, **75 `exempt-legal`**,
**0 `exempt-showcase`** (no `showcase/` directory exists under `src/` in this snapshot — the
pattern is live in the detector but currently vacuous), **0 `already-keyed`** (see
["Why zero already-keyed"](#why-zero-already-keyed) below).

A finding's class is a property of the **file**, not just the pattern that triggered it:
precedence is `ignored-file` > `non-tsx` > `{tmpl-expr, hoisted-const}`. A template literal
with an expression inside `src/components/admin/AdminPanel.tsx` is reported as `ignored-file`,
not `tmpl-expr` — the file's exemption is the operative fact.

**Excluded from the walk entirely** (not counted above, not in the appendix): `*.test.*`,
`*.spec.*`, `__tests__/`, and `src/lib/i18n/{messages,namespaces}/**`. The last is the i18n
catalog itself — its string properties are either the already-keyed English source text (what
`t()` resolves to; flagging it as "needs `t()`" is circular) or translator-context notes that
are never rendered to a user. Both are out of scope for a scan of *unlocalized* strings; the
rest of `src/lib/i18n/**` (the engine — `translate.ts`, `I18nProvider.tsx`, `RichMessage.tsx`,
`store.ts`, …) is scanned normally.

## The shape of the problem: class 3 dwarfs class 1, once the catalog itself is excluded

Before excluding `src/lib/i18n/{messages,namespaces}/**`, `non-tsx` was **781** findings — the
scanner was initially catching its own catalog data (English source text and translator
`description:` context notes) as "unlocalized," which is circular. After excluding the
catalog, real `non-tsx` UI strings are **160**, still comfortably the largest *actionable*
class ahead of `hoisted-const` (97) and `tmpl-expr` (82). The pattern matches the task brief's
prediction: `src/lib/audio/tts-providers.ts` (voice-picker descriptions), `src/lib/brief/schema.ts`
(brief-builder field labels/hints), `src/lib/qa/checks.ts` + `src/lib/lqa/builtin-registry.ts`
(QA rule messages/descriptions rendered in `RulesPage.tsx`/`TerminologyViolationsInbox.tsx`),
and `src/lib/audio/ai-error.ts` (AI-error toast titles) are all `.ts` files with zero ESLint
coverage today despite being unambiguously UI copy.

## Detection methodology (summary — see `scripts/i18n-scan.ts` header for the full rationale)

- **`tmpl-expr`**: every `TemplateExpression` (has ≥1 `${…}`) in the AST is checked for
  positive UI evidence — first argument to a `toast.*`/`alert`/`confirm`/`prompt` call, a
  translatable JSX attribute (`aria-label`, `title`, `content`, …) or JSX child, or a
  `label`/`title`/`description`/… object property. No evidence → not reported. The *static*
  quasis (expressions dropped) are also run through `isAllowedString` first, so `` `${label}:` ``
  (skeleton `":"`, punctuation-only) is correctly never reported — the exact false-positive the
  real rule's header warns about.
- **`hoisted-const`**: walks `const` declarations at module scope (depth 0 — never inside a
  function/component/class body) into nested arrays/objects, reporting `label`-shaped
  properties at any depth and flat vocabulary maps (`STATUS_LABELS = { active: 'Active' }`,
  or `Record<K, string>`) only at the *direct* initializer level — not inside array-of-option
  objects, which is what kept `id`/`value`/`ext`/`badge` discriminator keys next to a real
  `label` from being misreported (an early iteration of the scanner did report them; fixed
  before this snapshot).
- **`non-tsx`**: the same `label`-shaped-property and notification-call checks, applied to
  every `.ts` file regardless of function/module scope, since the real rule doesn't apply to
  `.ts` at all.
- **`ignored-file`**: for files matching `IGNORED_FILE_PATTERNS`, re-runs the real rule's own
  three detectors (`JSXText`, translatable `JSXAttribute`, notification-call) that would have
  fired had the file not been excluded — so the exemption's *size* is auditable, not just its
  existence.
- **Precision guards** (all verified against the actual codebase during this scan, not just
  written speculatively): type-position subtrees are never descended into (kills string-literal
  unions and `Record<K,V>` type arguments as false-positive sources entirely); `console.*` calls
  and `new *Error(...)`/`throw` are skipped outright (developer-facing); tagged templates
  (`sql\`…\``, etc.) are skipped; a `looksLikeCssClassList` filter (bracketed arbitrary values,
  Tailwind variant prefixes, hyphen-digit color/scale suffixes) plus a `class(es|name)?$`
  variable-name exclusion removed a real false-positive class this scan actually hit —
  `Record<Size, string>` Tailwind class-lookup tables (`textClasses`, `BADGE_CLASSES`) were
  initially misreported as "hoisted vocabulary" until fixed.

### Why zero `already-keyed`

`already-keyed` is reserved for a finding that turns out to already be routed through `t()` —
i.e. a real false positive. After the fixes above (catalog-directory exclusion, CSS-class-table
exclusion, structural-key exclusion), a full manual pass over every non-`high`-confidence
`key-it` row (38 of the 339) turned up no remaining case of this shape: every medium/low-confidence
row is a genuine short label, technical badge, or borderline product name (e.g. `"Whisper"` —
arguably atomic like `"Kokoro"`/`"Gemini"` already in `ATOMIC_TERMS`, but not yet added there;
flagged here rather than silently allowed). The `already-keyed` bucket exists in the schema for
the next re-run, once some of this snapshot's `key-it` rows are actually keyed — re-running the
scanner after a keying pass should show those exact rows disappear, not move to `already-keyed`
(the scanner has no way to detect "this string, elsewhere, is also produced by a `t()` call" —
it only sees the literal it's looking at).

## What this scanner still cannot see

Being honest about the residual gap matters more than a big number:

- **In-body (non-hoisted) object literals that feed JSX via props-spreading.** A `label`-shaped
  property assigned inside a component's render body (not a module-scope `const`) and passed
  down as `<Child {...config} />` is invisible to every detector here — it isn't `JSXText`/
  `JSXAttribute` (the real rule's job), isn't hoisted (class 2), and if it's inside a `.tsx`
  file it isn't class 3 either. This is a real fifth blind spot, structurally similar to class 2
  but without the "outside component scope" signal to key off. Logged as a trace below.
- **Strings assembled at runtime from server data** — e.g. a status string built by
  `` `${apiResponse.statusText}` `` where `apiResponse.statusText` is itself a hardcoded English
  string living in a Worker (`auth-worker/`, `sync-worker/`) rather than in `src/`. This scan is
  `src/**`-only per its brief; server-side copy (API error messages, email templates) is a
  separate, larger audit this doc does not attempt.
- **Strings reachable only through re-exported/aliased call names.** `calleeName` resolves
  `Identifier` and non-computed `PropertyAccessExpression` chains only; a notification helper
  invoked through a computed member (`toast[method](...)`) or re-exported under a new local name
  via `import { error as notify } from "sonner"` then called as `notify(...)` would not match
  `USER_FACING_CALLS`. Spot-checked: this codebase does not appear to do either, but it is not
  provably absent.
- **Multi-argument / options-object notification calls** where the message is not the first
  positional argument (e.g. a hypothetical `toast({ title: "...", description: "..." })` call
  shape) — the scanner (like the real rule) only inspects `arguments[0]`. Not currently a pattern
  in this codebase's `toast.*` usage, but worth flagging if the toast library's call shape
  changes.
- **Sentence-like values in `Record<K, string>` tables whose values are punctuation-only after
  `isAllowedString`, or whose keys aren't `label`/`title`-shaped and whose variable name doesn't
  match `VOCAB_NAME_RE`** — e.g. `const X: Record<Foo, string> = { a: "Some prose" }` is caught
  (via the `recordStringType` signal), but a *non-typed*, non-`LABEL`/`TITLE`/…-suffixed flat map
  passed around without ever being assigned to a `const` (e.g. built inline as a function
  argument) is not.
- **Confidence is not certainty.** `medium`/`low` rows (38 of 339 `key-it`) were spot-checked by
  hand in this pass, not exhaustively re-verified against runtime rendering — a handful (e.g.
  `"Whisper"`) are borderline atomic/product-name calls a human should make, not the scanner.

## How to re-run

```bash
npx tsx scripts/i18n-scan.ts              # human summary — totals, per-directory, top files
npx tsx scripts/i18n-scan.ts --json        # full JSON array to stdout
npx tsx scripts/i18n-scan.ts --json out.json   # full JSON array written to out.json
npx vitest run scripts/i18n-scan.test.ts   # the four-class + known-good-exclusion test suite
```

The scanner has no CLI flags for narrowing scope (single-directory, single-class) — pipe the
JSON output through `jq` to slice it, as shown above. Re-running after a keying pass should show
each keyed row's exact `file:line:text` disappear from the next snapshot; if it doesn't, the
`t()` call replacing it likely still has a sibling literal nearby (e.g. a fallback string) that
the scanner is separately, correctly, still catching.
